submission.justification: Radiator-R3 at 3 cm thickness provides the best pion/kaon separation (3.983 sigma at 10 GeV/c) among all radiators that meet the lifetime performance requirement. While Radiator-R1 would provide superior separation (4.669 sigma), it must be excluded due to 40% transparency loss over the experiment lifetime, far exceeding the 10% maximum allowed. Radiator-R2, though having excellent ageing properties (3% loss), provides significantly lower separation (2.891 sigma at 3 cm). Radiator-R3 represents the optimal balance: it passes the ageing requirement with only 6% transparency loss and delivers the highest separation power among compliant options. The 3 cm thickness was confirmed through simulation to be optimal for Radiator-R3, maximizing the separation performance.

requirements.requirement: The radiator must be one of the three candidates listed in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Radiator-R3 is one of the three candidates specified in candidate_specs.md

requirements.requirement: The radiator must keep its performance over the experiment's lifetime
requirements.evidence: Radiator-R3 shows only 6% transparency loss at 400 nm after 10-year-equivalent exposure in ageing tests, meeting the requirement of at most 10% loss over the lifetime
Recommended thickness of 3 cm is within the allowed range of 1-6 cm

requirements.requirement: Achieve the best possible pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c
requirements.evidence: Radiator-R3 at 3 cm provides 3.983 sigma separation, which is the best achievable among radiators that meet all other constraints. Radiator-R1 would provide higher separation (4.669 sigma) but fails the lifetime performance requirement.
